parameters.ref.semantic: an ARRAY is merged — how a custom component merges its internal ref with props.ref (no forwardRef needed in React 19)

parameters.state.semantic: passed as 2nd arg to the render callback AND auto-converted to data-* attributes

parameters.stateAttributesMapping.semantic: custom state->data-* mapping, e.g. { isActive: (v) => v ? { 'data-is-active': '' } : null }

parameters.props.semantic: merged with internal props: handlers merged, className/style joined, other external props overwrite internal ones

dataAttributes: None of its own — it converts component `state` keys into data-* attributes on the rendered element; this is the mechanism behind every Base UI data-* attribute.
renderProp: This hook IS the render-prop implementation for author components: `const element = useRender({ defaultTagName: 'p', ref: internalRef, state, stateAttributesMapping, props, render })`. Pair with mergeProps; nesting guidance in the composition handbook.
notableDifferences: React Aria components expose className/style render-state objects; useRender is how a custom component accepts the same `render` contract as Base UI parts. Migrating a RAC wrapper that forwards className/style is done with useRender, not cloneElement.
mergeProps + useRender replaces the repo's cloneElement/asChild patterns (pagination-base.tsx, carousel-base.tsx, buttons/button.tsx).
